questions.stem: Anaerobic bacteria are intrinsically resistant to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Aminoglycosides
  • Aminoglycosides is a medicinal and bacteriologic category of traditioal Gram-negative antibacterial medications that inhibit protein synthesis and contain as a portion of the molecule an amino-modified glycoside (sugar).

questions.stem: Niacin is given cautiously in insulin resistant diabetic patients because:

options.label: A
options.text: It hinders metabolism of diabetic drugs

options.label: B
options.text: It causes scleroderma hindering administration of insulin

questions.solutionHtml:
It causes hyperglycemia
  • Nicotinic Acid (Niacin): It is a B group vitamin which in much higher doses reduces plasma lipids. This action is unrelated to its vitamin activity and not present in nicotinamide. When nicotinic acid is given, TGs and VLDL decrease rapidly, followed by a modest fall in LDL-CH and total CH. A 20–50% reduction in plasma TGs and 15–25% reduction in CH levels has been recorded.

questions.stem: Sacubitril is a:
questions.solutionHtml:
Neprilysin inhibitor
  • Signed with the aim of developing analgesic and antihypertensive agents that act by preventing neprilysin's activity against signaling peptides such as enkephalins, substance P, endothelin, and atrial natriuretic peptide.

questions.stem: Antihypertensive contraindicated in PIH:
questions.solutionHtml:
Atenolol

Hypertension in pregnancy: A sustained BP reading above 140/90 mm Hg during pregnancy has implications both for the mother and the fetus—reduction of BP clearly reduces risks. Two types of situations are possible:

  1. A woman with pre-existing essential hypertension becomes pregnant.
  2. Pregnancy induced hypertension; as in toxemia of pregnancy—preeclampsia.
  • Toxemic hypertension is associated with a hyper adrenergic state, decrease in plasma volume (despite edema) and increase in vascular resistance.
  • In the first category the same therapy instituted before pregnancy may be continued.

questions.stem: Which of the following prolong Q-T interval?
questions.solutionHtml:
Quinidine
  • Quinidine is a class IA antiarrhythmic agent used to treat heart rhythm disturbances. It is the enantiomer of antimalarial agent quinine, originally derived from the bark of the cinchona tree. The drug causes increased action potential duration, as well as a prolonged QT interval

questions.stem: pKa is the pH at which?

options.label: A
options.text: 10 percent of the drug is ionized and 90 percent is non ionized

options.label: B
options.text: 50 percent of the drug is ionized and 50 percent is non ionized

options.label: C
options.text: 90 percent of the drug is ionized and 10 percent is non ionized

options.label: D
options.text: 100 percent of the drug is ionized

questions.answerText: 50 percent of the drug is ionized and 50 percent is non ionized
questions.solutionHtml:
50 percent of the drug is ionized and 50 percent is non ionized

Most drugs are weak electrolytes, i.e. their ionization is pH dependent (contrast strong electrolytes that are nearly completely ionized at acidic as well as alkaline pH). The ionization of a weak acid HA is given by the equation:

[A–]

  • pH = pKa + log [HA]

pKa is the negative logarithm of acidic dissociation constant of the weak electrolyte. If the concentration of ionized drug [A–] is equal to concentration of unionized drug [HA], then

[A–]

  • [HA] = 1

Since log 1 is 0, under this condition

  • pH = pKa

Thus, pKa is numerically equal to the pH at which the drug is 50% ionized.

questions.stem: Centrally acting muscle relaxant with alpha 2 adrenergic agonist activity is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tizanidine

Tizanidine: This clonidine congener is a central α 2 adrenergic agonists—inhibits release of excitatory amino acids in the spinal interneurons. It may facilitate the inhibitory transmitter glycine as well. Polysynaptic reflexes are inhibited resulting    in decreased muscle tone and frequency of muscle spasms without reducing muscle strength. Efficacy similar to baclofen or diazepam has been noted in multiple sclerosis, spinal injury and stroke, with fewer side effects.

questions.stem: All of the following drugs are bacteriostatic except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vancomycin
  • Vancomycin is an antibiotic used in the treatment of severe bacterial infections in hospitalized patients. It is effective against infections of the respiratory tract (e.g. pneumonia), urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, heart, blood, and others.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about prasugrel is true as compared to clopidogrel?

options.label: A
options.text: It is slower acting than clopidogrel

options.label: C
options.text: It is a reversible antagonist of ADP receptors

questions.solutionHtml:
It is contraindicated in stroke
  • ADP receptor antagonists: These include the thienopyridine (clopidogrel and prasugrel) and ticagrelor. All of these drugs target P2Y12, the key ADP receptor on platelets.
  • Mechanism of action: The thienopyridine are structurally related drugs that selectively inhibit ADP-induced platelet aggregation by irreversibly blocking P2Y12.

questions.stem: Serotonin is chemically?
questions.solutionHtml:
5-hydroxytryptamine
  • 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT, Serotonin): Serotonin was the name given to the vasoconstrictor substance which appeared in the serum when blood clotted and Enteramine to the smooth muscle contracting substance present in enterochromaffin cells of gut mucosa. In the early 1950s both were shown to be 5-hydroxy- tryptamine (5-HT).

questions.stem: Pirenzepine is used for:
questions.solutionHtml:
Gastric ulcer

Peptic ulcers are open sores that develop on the inside lining of your stomach and the upper portion of your small intestine. The most common symptom of a peptic ulcer is stomach pain.
